intro.say: A habitat is the kind of place where an animal lives and finds food. Let us visit some!

rounds.say: A desert is very hot and dry, with lots of sand. Camels and lizards live there.
rounds.caption: desert

rounds.say: The ocean is a huge salty sea. Fish, whales and octopuses live in the water.
rounds.caption: ocean

rounds.say: The Arctic is icy and freezing cold. Polar bears and seals live on the ice and snow.
rounds.caption: Arctic

rounds.ask: Which animal lives in the ocean?

options.label: camel
options.why: A camel lives in the hot, dry desert.

options.label: polar bear
options.why: A polar bear lives on the icy Arctic snow.

rounds.explain: Fish swim and breathe in the water, so the ocean is their habitat.

rounds.ask: A polar bear lives where it is…

options.label: hot and sandy
options.why: A polar bear would get far too hot in the desert.

options.label: in the sea only
options.why: Polar bears swim, but they live on the ice too.

rounds.explain: Polar bears have thick fur to stay warm on the Arctic ice.

rounds.ask: Which place is a hot, dry desert?

options.label: ocean
options.why: The ocean is full of water, not dry at all.

options.label: ice
options.why: Ice is freezing cold, not hot.

rounds.explain: A desert has lots of sand, sunshine and very little rain.

rounds.ask: Help each animal get home. Desert or ocean?
rounds.explain: Camels, scorpions and lizards like hot sand. Whales, octopuses and sharks need the sea.

intro.say: Let us meet the rainforest and the grassland too, and help animals find the right home.

rounds.say: A rainforest is hot and very rainy, with tall trees close together. Monkeys, parrots and frogs live there.
rounds.caption: rainforest

rounds.say: A grassland is a wide open land covered in grass. Lions, zebras and giraffes live there.
rounds.caption: grassland

rounds.ask: Monkeys swing from tree to tree. Which habitat suits them best?

options.label: desert
options.why: The desert has very few trees to climb.

options.label: Arctic
options.why: The Arctic is icy with no tall trees.

rounds.explain: The rainforest is full of tall trees, perfect for climbing monkeys.

rounds.ask: Where do zebras run and eat grass?

options.label: ocean
options.why: Zebras cannot live in the water.

options.label: rainforest
options.why: The trees are too thick for zebras to run.

rounds.explain: Grasslands give zebras plenty of grass to eat and space to run.

rounds.ask: Which animal lives in the rainforest?

options.label: camel
options.why: Camels live in the dry desert.

options.label: seal
options.why: Seals live in cold seas and on the ice.

options.label: whale
options.why: Whales live in the ocean.

rounds.explain: Parrots live high in rainforest trees and eat the fruit there.

rounds.ask: Rainforest or grassland? Sort the animals.
rounds.explain: Tree climbers live in the rainforest; grazers and runners live on the grassland.

rounds.ask: Three homes! Where does each animal live?
rounds.explain: Each animal lives where it can find food and stay safe.

intro.say: Animal bodies are just right for their habitat. Let us find out why!

rounds.say: A camel stores fat in its hump and can go many days without drinking. Wide feet stop it sinking in sand.
rounds.caption: camel: desert

rounds.say: A polar bear has thick fur and a layer of fat to keep warm. Fish have gills to breathe underwater.
rounds.caption: fur for cold, gills for water

rounds.ask: Why can a polar bear live in the freezing Arctic?

options.label: It drinks hot water
options.why: There is no hot water on the ice!

options.label: It sleeps all day
options.why: Sleeping does not keep it warm by itself.

rounds.explain: Thick fur and a layer of fat keep the polar bear warm in the cold.

rounds.ask: Which body part helps a fish live in the ocean?

options.label: fur
options.why: Fur would get soggy; fish do not need it.

options.label: a hump
options.why: A hump helps camels in the desert.

rounds.explain: Gills let a fish take oxygen from the water so it can breathe.

rounds.ask: A cactus stores water inside it. Which habitat is it made for?

options.label: rainforest
options.why: The rainforest is so rainy that plants do not need to store water.

options.label: Arctic
options.why: A cactus would freeze in the Arctic.

options.label: ocean
options.why: A cactus cannot grow in salty seawater.

rounds.explain: Deserts get very little rain, so storing water helps the cactus survive.

rounds.ask: A frog needs wet places and lots of insects to eat. Where would it be happiest?

options.label: desert
options.why: The desert is too dry for a frog’s wet skin.

options.label: Arctic
options.why: It is far too cold for a frog there.

rounds.explain: The rainforest is warm, wet and full of insects, just right for frogs.

rounds.ask: If a camel was taken to the Arctic, what would happen?

options.label: It would love it
options.why: Its body is made for heat, not ice.

options.label: It would grow fins
options.why: Animals cannot grow new body parts like that.

rounds.explain: A desert camel's body is made for heat, so the icy Arctic would be far too cold.

rounds.ask: Where do they live? Think about their bodies!
rounds.explain: Desert animals handle heat, sea animals swim and breathe in water, Arctic animals stay warm.
